title: Director of Technical Services

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: This role provides technical support, customer training, and application expertise for Canon's large-format printer customers. They directly handle customer pain points around print durability, outdoor performance issues, and material selection guidance. Tedlar solves their operational challenges: (1) Support ticket reduction - customer complaints about UV fading, cracking, or premature graphic failure on Canon-printed materials decrease when protected with Tedlar's proven 60+ year track record; (2) Technical credibility - Tedlar's extreme temperature range (-70°F to 230°F), mold/mildew resistance, and graffiti resistance provide concrete specifications they can recommend during customer consultations for challenging applications; (3) Application enablement - they can confidently recommend Tedlar for vehicle wraps, architectural graphics, and outdoor signage knowing it will perform for 12-20+ years, protecting Canon's reputation when customers use their Colorado UVgel or Arizona flatbed output. Given Canon's 3M MCS Warranty certification focus and emphasis on durable media offerings, Technical Services needs trusted protective film partners to recommend for applications where customers demand maximum longevity and reduced maintenance costs.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: The Director of Technical Services owns customer-facing technical support, training programs, and application best practices for Canon's large-format printing portfolio (Colorado M-series, Arizona flatbed, imagePROGRAF). They influence material and finishing specifications recommended to customers, develop technical documentation, and directly field support tickets related to print durability and outdoor performance failures. This role reports to senior operations or customer success leadership and manages technical support engineers and application specialists. They don't make purchasing decisions but are critical influencers in the materials ecosystem—what they recommend to customers becomes de facto standard practice.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Three Tedlar use cases matter most to this role: (1) Vehicle wrap protection for Colorado M-series UVgel output—Tedlar prevents UV degradation and scratching on fleet graphics and wraps where Canon touts weather resistance and vibrant color retention; (2) Outdoor signage overlaminates for Arizona flatbed-printed architectural and building graphics—Tedlar's graffiti resistance and extreme temperature performance (-70°F to 230°F) solve the harsh condition challenges Canon markets; (3) Transit and architectural interior applications where Canon's water-resistant media is used—Tedlar adds a protective layer ensuring surfaces remain clean and durable despite high-touch environments. Each use case reduces support tickets, extends the performance claims Canon makes about their printers, and protects Canon's brand when customers deploy graphics in demanding environments.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This role likely owns KPIs around support ticket volume/resolution time, customer satisfaction scores (CSAT/NPS), technical training effectiveness, and first-call resolution rates. Their personal pain points include recurring complaints about print fading, cracking, or premature failure on outdoor applications—issues that damage Canon's reputation and create repeat support burden. They care about having reliable, spec-driven solutions they can confidently recommend during customer consultations. Tedlar's value propositions directly benefit them: UV protection eliminates fading complaints, graffiti resistance solves vandalism issues on architectural projects, and the proven track record gives them technical credibility when advising on challenging applications. Success for them means fewer escalations, happier customers who get results matching Canon's durability marketing, and a trusted partner specification that protects Canon's quality positioning.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Canon is currently in a high-activity phase with recent Colorado XL-series global debut at PRINTING United Expo 2025 (October in Orlando), Colorado M-series enhancements launched April 2025, and ongoing 3M MCS Warranty certification emphasis. Technical Services is likely fielding questions about optimal finishing and protection solutions for these new printer capabilities. Canon's title sponsorship of PRINTING United 2025 and active showcase of vehicle wrap/outdoor signage applications creates urgency—customers are asking about how to maximize outdoor performance, and Technical Services needs authoritative answers. Additionally, Canon's focus on harsh condition applications and weather-resistant media in their marketing means Technical Services is under pressure to deliver on these durability promises with validated material recommendations.

personalization_hooks.hook: Technical Services likely handles recurring support tickets about print longevity on vehicle wraps and architectural graphics where customers expect multi-year performance based on Canon's marketing claims
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame the conversation around support ticket reduction and technical credibility—offer Tedlar as a spec they can confidently recommend that prevents the fading, cracking, and maintenance complaints they currently manage

personalization_hooks.hook: Canon's 3M MCS Warranty certification and partnership with material suppliers demonstrates their commitment to validated, tested solutions for customer applications
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar's proven performance data and specific technical specs (temperature range, graffiti resistance, UV stability) as the kind of validated solution that aligns with Canon's quality standards and gives Technical Services concrete guidance for customer consultations

recommended_approach: Lead with support efficiency and technical credibility angle—position Tedlar as solving recurring customer pain points they're already managing (UV degradation, outdoor performance failures). Emphasize concrete technical specifications and proven performance data that gives them confidence in recommendations. Frame as a partnership to protect Canon's quality reputation and reduce support burden, not a sales pitch.
